lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.criterion: Safe export metadata and expected-output boundary
findings.observation: The Opik projection path allowlists top-level fields, but it still exports free-form metadata strings from projectName, datasetName, trace eventKind/status/reasonCode, terminalReasonCode, and score reasonCode. The export scanner blocks emails, phone numbers, secrets, absolute paths, and some forbidden field names, but it does not block candidate names, oracle text, or other sensitive narrative carried inside otherwise allowed strings.
findings.evidence: apps/eval-runner/src/safeExportPolicy.ts:34-63 and 150-190 allow and export projectName, datasetName, trace, scores, and terminalReasonCode; apps/eval-runner/src/safeExportPolicy.ts:92-113 only scans strings for email/phone/path/secret patterns; packages/evaluation/src/contracts.ts:398-408 leaves SafeEvaluationTraceV1 eventKind/status/reasonCode as unconstrained strings; apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikTransport.ts:220-297 turns datasetName into experimentName and exports trace and score reason strings; apps/eval-runner/src/safeExportPolicy.test.ts:8-38 only covers email/phone/path/secret cases.
findings.user_impact: A future scenario, executor, or operator-supplied name can leak expected-output hints or relationship identifiers into Opik while the system still reports a safe allowlisted projection. That weakens both privacy controls and evaluator blindness.
findings.recommendation: Constrain exported metadata to bounded enums or slug-safe digests, derive experiment and dataset labels from repository IDs instead of free text, and extend export validation to detect oracle tokens and human-identifying narrative in all exported metadata strings.
findings.verification: Add a failing test where projectName, datasetName, trace.reasonCode, or score.reasonCode contains oracle text or a synthetic candidate label; projection should be rejected before any SDK call.

findings.observation: The deletion flow marks an Opik projection as deleted after deleting the trace and confirming that the trace endpoint returns not found, but it does not verify that experiment links or other remote projection remnants are gone. The proof validator repeats that same narrow check, so the current receipt overstates what was actually read back.
findings.evidence: apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikTransport.ts:249-256 inserts dataset-item to trace links into an experiment; apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikTransport.ts:317-329 deletes and read-backs only the trace ID; apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikReporter.ts:204-245 emits OPIK_DELETE_READBACK_VERIFIED once projectionExists is false; scripts/evals/validate-evaluation-platform-proof.mjs:116-120 validates only the deletion receipt, not experiment or linkage cleanup.
findings.user_impact: Operators can believe a remote evaluation projection was fully deleted when only the trace lookup disappeared. Residual remote metadata would weaken retention and deletion guarantees and make later audits less truthful.
findings.recommendation: Either narrow the receipt claim to trace-level deletion or add remote readback for experiment membership and every stored projection surface that Talent Signal treats as part of the projection boundary.
findings.verification: After deletion, assert both trace absence and no remaining experiment item for the trace ID; if the API exposes scores, spans, feedback, or annotations separately, verify those surfaces are also absent before returning deleted.

strengths: The local manifest and gate artifact are written before optional projection, and projection failures do not flip the local gate result: apps/eval-runner/src/runSuite.ts:212-245 and 247-264; packages/evaluation/src/localJsonReporter.ts:93-223; apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikReporter.test.ts:103-131.

Repository scenarios keep model input, initial state, and oracle physically separate, and the repository validator/tests explicitly reject oracle leakage into model-visible input: evals/v2/README.md:15-25; apps/eval-runner/src/modeDispatch.ts:48-95; packages/evaluation/src/evaluation.test.ts:296-350.

The Opik path pins dataset digest and dataset version before starting a projection and records failure-recovery and deletion receipts in a local projection ledger: apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikTransport.ts:177-187; apps/eval-runner/src/projectionLedger.ts:72-183; scripts/evals/validate-evaluation-platform-proof.mjs:28-143.
missing_evidence: No adversarial test proves that projectName, datasetName, trace.reasonCode, terminalReasonCode, or score.reasonCode cannot carry oracle text or synthetic person identifiers through the export path.
No remote deletion proof shows experiment-link cleanup after trace deletion; the frozen proof only shows a deleted trace receipt and trace-level readback failure.
No end-to-end proof in this bundle shows how the Opik path behaves for non-shareable governed classes beyond the synthetic-only scenarios and owner-controlled smoke run.
open_questions: Should Opik-visible names become fully digest-derived so the projection path never depends on operator-supplied free text?
